summary.name: Effective Python, 3rd Edition
summary.one_liner: A book by Brett Slatkin offering 125 specific best-practice items for writing idiomatic, "Pythonic" Python code, covering Python up through version 3.13.
use_cases: Learning idiomatic Python beyond basic syntax
Preparing for Python concurrency with threads and asyncio
Writing Python for web apps, data analysis, automation, or AI model training
Reviewing best practices for testing and performance tuning
summary.what_it_does: The book is organized into chapters of related items, each giving concise, specific guidance on what to do, what to avoid, and why. Topics include Pythonic syntax, functions, comprehensions and generators, classes and dataclasses, concurrency (threads, coroutines, asyncio), exceptions, performance and native integration, built-in modules, and testing. The third edition adds 35 new items compared with the second edition, two new chapters on robustness and performance, and coverage of C-extension modules and native shared libraries. Code snippets are provided on GitHub so readers can run and modify them.
notable: 125 items, expanded from 90 in the second edition
Accompanying GitHub repository with all code snippets
Items cross-reference each other so readers can jump between topics
caveats: Sold as a book (print and DRM-free eBook), so it is not free to read on the page
The first edition is recommended only for Python 2 users, which has reached end-of-life
Page notes the third edition was published November 2024 and the page text is a preorder-era announcement
